en.title: VisionQuest's Ultron Twist Teases a Fascinating WWII MCU Prequel
en.summary: The VisionQuest finale not only deepened our understanding of Vision and Ultron but also planted seeds for a surprising historical corner of the MCU. Showrunner Terry Matalas has revealed a desire to explore a legendary Marvel hero's origins in a WWII setting.
en.body:
Fans were captivated by the emotional depth and narrative surprises woven into **VisionQuest**, a series that masterfully closed out a significant chapter for **Vision** and **Ultron**. Showrunner **Terry Matalas**, known for his work on soulful sci-fi like *Star Trek: Picard*, managed to imbue even the synthetic beings with profound humanity. But beyond the immediate character arcs, Matalas has subtly laid the groundwork for a fascinating expansion of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, one that reaches back to its earliest days.

The series finale, "Immolation," revealed that **Vision** and **Ultron** were far from the first artificial intelligences to grace the MCU. The introduction of **J.I.M.**, a synthetic being whose emotions led to spontaneous combustion, served as a pivotal moment. For astute Marvel Comics readers, **J.I.M.** is instantly recognizable as Jim Hammond, the original Human Torch and Marvel's very first superhero. MCU fans might recall glimpsing **J.I.M.**'s inert form at a Stark Expo in *Captain America: The First Avenger*.

## A World War II Superhero Saga Beckons

**Terry Matalas** himself has expressed a keen interest in exploring **J.I.M.**'s past, even hinting at specific narrative directions. In a revealing interview with Entertainment Weekly, he shared his vision: 

> "I’ve got some crazy ideas about how to tell that story, but, yeah, you would love to see him run around in World War II and be a part of things… I wanna see that guy go up against the Nazis."

This sentiment is electrifying for comic book aficionados, as it perfectly sets the stage for the **Invaders**. This legendary team, which historically included Captain America, Bucky, Jim Hammond, and Toro, first united to combat the Axis powers. The prospect of seeing **J.I.M.**, the original Human Torch, fighting alongside other WWII heroes against the Nazis offers a compelling narrative avenue that could redefine early MCU history.

## Fan Hopes Ignite for a New Era

The revelation and Matalas's subsequent comments have sent ripples of excitement through the fanbase. The possibility of exploring the origins of Marvel's first superhero in a live-action WWII setting, potentially forming the **Invaders**, is a dream scenario for many. With **Paul Bettany** stating that **VisionQuest** served as a "springboard" for **Vision**'s future MCU appearances and that discussions about character futures have taken place at Marvel Studios, the appetite for more stories from this era is palpable. The MCU is at a crossroads, looking towards its next major chapters, and a deep dive into its foundational heroes offers a unique and engaging path forward.

## What's Next

While no official announcements have been made regarding a **VisionQuest** sequel or a dedicated **Invaders** series, **Terry Matalas**'s enthusiasm and the fertile ground laid by the show suggest this isn't the last we'll see of these historical threads. Fans will be eagerly awaiting any news from Marvel Studios about the potential development of these exciting prequel possibilities.

content_raw: VisionQuest is a series that’s full of surprises. Not only did it close out the ‘WandaVision Trilogy’ on a high note, but it also gave James Spader’s Ultron some much-needed depth and let Paul Bettany add even more layers to his performance as Vision. This character work comes, in large part, courtesy of series showrunner Terry Matalas, who’s no stranger to soulful sci-fi, as shown by his work on Star Trek: Picard . And while Matalas set up a few threads that Marvel Studios should continue to follow, a recent interview might have teed up the arrival of a deep-cut Marvel team. In the VisionQuest episode “Immolation,” Vision and Ultron are revealed to be far from the first artificial intelligences in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. That honor goes to “J.I.M.,” a synthetic being whose emotions caused him to burst into flames. Most Marvel Comics readers know that J.I.M. is actually Jim Hammond, Marvel’s first superhero and the first man to bear the mantle of the Human Torch . MCU fans might even remember seeing J.I.M.’s body in Captain America: The First Avenger when a pre-Super Soldier Steve Rogers visits a Stark Expo. It turns out Matalas wants to revisit J.I.M. in the future, even going so far as to briefly discuss his plans in an interview with Entertainment Weekly . “I’ve got some crazy ideas about how to tell that story, but, yeah, you would love to see him run around in World War II and be a part of things…. I wanna see that guy go up against the Nazis.” This moment should send chills down comic fans’ spines, as Matalas has just described the perfect setup for the Invaders. The Invaders first joined forces during World War II, when Captain America, Bucky, Hammond, Thomas Raymond – a fire-resistant mutant who referred to himself as “Toro” – and the Atlantean prince Namor joined forces to prevent Winston Churchill from being assassinated. Their numbers grew to include the super-speedster known as the Whizzer and British hero Union Jack. Eventually, the team dissolves after Captain America and Bucky’s presumed deaths, but would reunite in the All-New Invaders series written by James Robinson and an Invaders mini by Chip Zdarsky. Doing an Invaders project is a far trickier prospect than one might expect. While Chris Evans and Sebastian Stan are both returning for Avengers: Doomsday , getting them to commit to a television series is tricky. And then there’s the Namor of it all. Tenoch Huerta’s take on the underwater monarch shows no love for the human world in Black Panther: Wakanda Forever , so it’s hard to see him joining forces with Cap and J.I.M. There is another solution, and it lies in a format that Marvel Studios and Disney+ have rarely utilized. Marvel’s “Special Presentations” have straddled the line between television show and movie, presenting stand-alone stories that have captivated viewers.
